metadata.title: Implement Comprehensive Error Handling and Observability for Dashboard Interactions

story.iWant: to be informed of errors during dashboard interactions and for these errors to be logged
story.soThat: I can understand issues quickly and the development team can diagnose and resolve problems efficiently.
story.tasks: - Define error states and corresponding user feedback mechanisms (e.g., toast notifications for critical errors, inline messages for validation). - Integrate a frontend error logging service (if not already present). - Implement error boundaries or similar mechanisms for robust UI error handling. - Refactor `DashboardManager` and other relevant services to capture and log errors. - Implement user-facing feedback for failed `updateSessionStatus` operations. - Ensure logging includes necessary context for debugging (e.g., `sessionId`, new status attempted).

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Critical errors during real-time subscription or data updates are displayed to the user as persistent, dismissible error messages. 2. Non-critical errors (e.g., minor data fetching issues) are logged to a frontend monitoring service without interrupting the user flow. 3. User receives clear, concise feedback for failed actions (e.g., status update failed). 4. Automated logging captures sufficient context (e.g., error type, component, timestamp, user ID) to diagnose issues.

artifact.title: Epic Technical Specification: Dashboard & Progress Tracking
artifact.snippet: Initial dashboard load should take less than 2 seconds, and UI updates less than 200ms. Error handling mechanisms should not degrade these performance targets.

artifact.title: Epic Technical Specification: Dashboard & Progress Tracking
artifact.snippet: The frontend should be able to handle temporary disconnects from the Supabase Realtime service and automatically re-subscribe, ensuring error feedback for such events is managed.

artifact.title: Epic Technical Specification: Dashboard & Progress Tracking
artifact.snippet: Log any errors during real-time subscription or status updates to a frontend monitoring service. This is a direct requirement for comprehensive observability.

constraint.description: Error handling and logging mechanisms should be optimized to avoid introducing performance bottlenecks in the dashboard interactions.
Error messages and logs must not expose sensitive user data or internal system details.
Robust error handling should improve the overall resilience of the application against various failure scenarios (e.g., network, API, data).
Logging should provide sufficient context (error type, component, timestamp, user ID) to diagnose issues efficiently without excessive noise.
Error handling patterns should align with Next.js best practices and seamlessly integrate with Supabase interaction models.
Error messages and feedback should adhere to the established Shadcn UI components and design patterns for consistency.

tests.standards: Unit Tests: Test specific error handling logic, error logging functions, and individual error boundary components in isolation. Component Tests: Test critical error display components, ensuring correct message rendering, dismiss behavior, and visual consistency with UI patterns. Integration/E2E Tests: Simulate various error scenarios (e.g., API failures, network disconnects, invalid data responses) to verify proper error display and logging across different dashboard interactions (loading, status updates, detail views). User Experience Testing: Validate that error messages are clear, concise, and actionable for end-users, and that non-critical errors do not disrupt workflow.
tests.locations: Typically `__tests__` or `tests` directories within relevant feature modules, or a dedicated `tests/error-handling` directory.

ideas.idea: Verify critical real-time subscription errors trigger a persistent, dismissible toast notification.
Test that minor data fetching issues are logged to the frontend monitoring service without displaying a disruptive message to the user.
Simulate a failed `updateSessionStatus` call and verify the user receives appropriate feedback (e.g., a temporary inline error message or revert of optimistic update).
Examine logs in the monitoring service to ensure captured errors include necessary context (e.g., component name, timestamp, user ID, error stack).
Test the behavior of `ErrorBoundary` components, ensuring they catch render errors and display a fallback UI.
